meta.description: Not Douglas Adams. The line is Rick Cook's, from his 1989 novel The Wizardry Compiled — Wikiquote sources it, and Adams's own page has no trace of it.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Programming today is a race between software engineers striving to build bigger and better idiot-proof programs, and the Universe trying to produce bigger and better idiots. So far, the Universe is winning'?
meta.ogDescription: Rick Cook wrote it in The Wizardry Compiled (Baen, 1989). Douglas Adams never did — the sentence appears nowhere on his Wikiquote page, and no source names a book.

answer.label: Not Douglas Adams — actually Rick Cook
answer.authorDates: 1944–2022 · American fantasy novelist & Analog science-fact writer
answer.sourceLine: The line is Rick Cook’s, from The Wizardry Compiled, the second of his comic Wizardry novels about a programmer stranded in a world that runs on magic, published by Baen Books in December 1989. English Wikiquote prints it word for word under that book; Douglas Adams’s own Wikiquote page does not contain the sentence, or the word “idiot,” anywhere.

source.heading: The book it comes from

docMeta.dd: Douglas Adams — unsourced, and absent from his own Wikiquote page

source.excerpt: Programming today is a race between software engineers striving to build bigger and better idiot-proof programs, and the Universe trying to produce bigger and better idiots. So far, the Universe is winning.
trail: English Wikiquote prints the sentence word for word in its Rick Cook entry ↗, under a heading for The Wizardry Compiled (1989), among other computing jokes from the same novel.

Wikipedia’s article on Rick Cook ↗ dates the book from the Locus index: Baen Books, December 1989, ISBN 0-671-69856-7, the sequel to Wizard’s Bane. A library record for a later Baen printing, scanned at the Internet Archive ↗, carries 1991 and notes an original publication of 1990 — a printing difference, not a different book.

The line is not on the Douglas Adams side of the ledger. His Wikiquote page ↗ is arranged strictly by work and, read in its raw page source, contains no instance of “idiot,” “programming today” or “universe is winning.”

Quote Investigator’s Douglas Adams file ↗ lists seven investigations into sayings pinned on him — the raindrop and the flood, all of Bach streamed into space, forty-two — and this quotation is not one of them. A search of the site for “bigger and better idiots” returns nothing, so no specialist verdict is being contradicted or borrowed here.
source.excerptNote: Wikiquote lists this among the quotations from the novel, but the book is available online only as a lending scan, so its exact placement and page could not be checked here and none is claimed. Wikiquote characterises Cook’s writing as containing “many computer jokes,” and “best enjoyed by those who have a background in computers” — which is the company this sentence keeps on the page, alongside gags about segmented memory architecture and shipping something because “this is only version 1.0.”

author.name: Rick Cook
author.kicker: The man who actually wrote it
author.heading: Rick Cook, the programmer’s novelist
author.metaLine: 1944–2022 · American fantasy novelist & Analog science-fact writer
author.bio: James Richard Cook (1944–2022) was an American science fiction and fantasy author whose best-known books are the Wizardry series, beginning with Wizard’s Bane in January 1989. Wikiquote describes his writing as full of computer jokes and “best enjoyed by those who have a background in computers” — a fair summary of novels whose hero solves magical problems by debugging them. Alongside the fiction he wrote science-fact pieces for Analog on computing subjects, including “Neural Nets” in 1989 and “Cyberspaced Out: Manners and Mores in the Global Village” in 1992.

misattribution.heading: Who it gets pinned on, and why
misattribution.intro: This is a programmer’s joke that acquired a famous author. Two distinct errors circulate — one swaps the writer entirely, the other only mangles his name.

items.why: Aggregators file the identical sentence under Adams with no book, no page and no date: Goodreads ↗ shows it under his name beneath its own notice that community quotes are unverified. His Wikiquote page ↗, which is organised work by work, does not contain the sentence — nor the word “idiot” — anywhere in its page source.
Several quotation databases reach the right man and then get his first name wrong: Quotes.net prints it under “Rich Cook” ↗, with no source book named. The author is Rick Cook — James Richard Cook.

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence was written by Rick Cook and published in The Wizardry Compiled (Baen Books, December 1989), where Wikiquote sources it word for word ↗.

context.heading: Why this one sticks to Douglas Adams
lead: It is a very good joke, and it sounds like a very good joke Douglas Adams would have made. He wrote at length about computers, he loved them noisily and in public, and his comic register — a cosmic-scale straight face, the Universe cast as an active participant with a sense of humour — is exactly the register this sentence is written in. That resemblance is doing all the work. It is why the line drifted, and it is not evidence of anything.

What the line actually is, is an in-joke from inside the profession. Rick Cook’s Wizardry novels drop a working programmer into a fantasy world and let him treat spellcasting as a software problem; Wikiquote’s page for him is a run of gags about segmented memory architecture, version 1.0 and whether a thing is a bug or a feature. “So far, the Universe is winning” belongs to that book, not to the Hitchhiker’s canon.
context.detailsSummary: How the credit drifted, and what can and cannot be shown
detailsBody: No source has ever been attached to the Adams version. Goodreads files the sentence under Adams ↗ with no book, page or year, above its own standing warning that community-added quotes are not verified; QuotePark does the same ↗ while listing an identical quote credited to Rick Cook, The Wizardry Compiled (1989), a few lines further down its own page. The two attributions sit side by side and only one of them names a book.

Exactly when or how the shift happened is not documented anywhere this page could confirm, so no origin story for the misattribution is asserted here. What can be shown is the negative: the sentence is absent from Adams’s Wikiquote entry, and absent from Quote Investigator’s Douglas Adams file, which contains seven investigations and not this one.
context.pull: Adams wrote a great deal about computers. He did not write this.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Rick Cook page prints the exact sentence under a heading for The Wizardry Compiled (1989), and describes his writing as containing many computer jokes, best enjoyed by those with a computing background.

Wikipedia dates The Wizardry Compiled to Baen Books, December 1989, ISBN 0-671-69856-7, sequel to Wizard's Bane; gives Rick Cook's dates as 1944 to January 13, 2022; and lists his Analog science-fact articles including 'Neural Nets' (1989) and 'Cyberspaced Out' (1992).

Douglas Adams's Wikiquote page is organised by work and contains no occurrence of 'idiot', 'programming today' or 'universe is winning'; its only top-level sections are Quotes, Quotes about Adams and External links.
Goodreads attributes the exact sentence to Douglas Adams with no source book or date, above a notice that community-added quotes are not verified by Goodreads.
Goodreads' quotes page for the work The Wizardry Compiled carries the exact sentence attributed to Rick Cook, The Wizardry Compiled.
QuotePark attributes the sentence to Douglas Adams with no source given, while listing an identical quote credited to Rick Cook, The Wizardry Compiled (1989), among its related quotes.
Quotes.net prints the sentence under the misspelled name 'Rich Cook' and names no source book.
The Quotations Page attributes the sentence to Rick Cook, The Wizardry Compiled.
Quote Investigator's Douglas Adams tag page lists seven investigations, none of which concerns 'idiot-proof programs' or 'bigger and better idiots'.
The Internet Archive holds a scanned, lending-restricted Baen printing of The Wizardry Compiled by Rick Cook, catalogued 1991 with a note that it was originally published New York: Baen, 1990.
A site search of quoteinvestigator.com for 'bigger and better idiots' returns no results, confirming QI has no article on this quotation.
Douglas Adams was an English author, humourist and screenwriter, 1952 to 2001.
